name: Chiamaka Ferreira-Wolff
creator: Chiamaka Ferreira-Wolff
description: Ferreira-Wolff operates the Marrow Gallery, a semi-legal exhibition space in the Shelf's lower corridors that serves as the primary venue for unregistered art in GLMZ's underground scene — but she is also, under the pseudonym 'Ache,' one of its most significant exhibiting artists. Her own work consists of large-format physical collages assembled from corporate waste: shredded documents, packaging from Tier 4 consumer goods, obsolete BCI packaging, and discarded geneware applicators, arranged into dense, overwhelming grids that she calls 'consumption portraits.' She has never publicly confirmed the Ache identity.
medium: physical collage / found corporate material / gallery space
cultural_impact: The Marrow Gallery has launched more than forty artists who now have significant presence in GLMZ's cultural landscape, making Ferreira-Wolff arguably more influential as a curator and space-holder than as an artist — though the Ache works command serious gray-market prices among Tier 3 collectors who suspect the connection.
controversy: Municipal authorities have attempted to close the Marrow Gallery six times on various pretexts; each closure has been reversed through community pressure and legal support from the Seam Rights advocacy network. The Ache identity, if confirmed, would expose Ferreira-Wolff to corporate defamation suits from several companies whose waste materials she uses.
story_hooks: A piece of shredded document in one of the Ache collages, partially legible, appears to contain evidence of a significant corporate crime — and someone has noticed.

A Tier 4 collector has purchased every available Ache work and is now attempting to 'donate' them to a corporate museum, which would require Ache to be publicly identified for the gift to be legally processed.
Ferreira-Wolff has asked a trusted person to take over the Marrow Gallery — and left behind a sealed room containing works she has never shown anyone.
